theorem.statement: The answer to the differential-inverse question is affirmative.  For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), every observed-data DQM score admits a measurable conditional-\(X\), uniformly bounded lift to factorwise centered additive latent scores.  The lift uses \(\mathfrak I_0\) for the finite differentiated factors, the conditional \(G(X)^+\) solve for measurement scores, and the pointwise \(\{R^{\mathsf T}DR\}^{-1}\) solve for the residual propensity and support-preserving class-density scores.
theorem.proof_tex: The asserted statement is exactly the statement of theorem thm:differential-inverse-resolution.  Apply that theorem.  Its proof basis is theorem thm:differential-score-lifting, whose equations (79)--(94) construct the measurable conditional-\(X\), uniformly bounded lift, verify every factorwise centering condition, and establish support preservation for the class-density score.  Thus the existing canonical theorem answers the open-ended question affirmatively, with no additional hypothesis or mathematical claim.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), every observed-data DQM score has a measurable conditional-\(X\), uniformly bounded, support-preserving lift to centered additive latent-factor scores. Hence the full observed tangent closure is the latent score-image closure, and the exact continuous-outcome canonical gradient is obtained by a pointwise \(K^2\)-cell projection followed by one conditional Gram solve. The implementable score uses one non-oracle fitted product law, a computable spectral cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), and explicit support-leakage allowances; efficient cross-fitted Gaussian and maximum-\(t\) inference requires the stated operator, screening, leakage, and product-rate conditions.

project_justification.fill: The project differentiates the separated three-view factorization and proves a measurable uniformly bounded right inverse from every observed DQM score to factorwise centered latent additive scores, including support-preserving recovery of the class-density score. This closes tangent-space completeness and validates the finite projector as the canonical correction. The attaining estimator is non-oracle: a fixed \(\varepsilon/2\) spectral cutoff selects the fitted Gram directions on the separated event, while estimable low-mass diagnostics expose structural-zero leakage in the remainder and inference conditions.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) are the closest theorem-level comparator: their Theorems 2--4 treat the binary observed tangent space and influence functions, and Supplement S8.2 obtains the continuous-outcome efficiency bound through a refining outcome partition. The present multilevel construction instead proves a conditional differential score lift and uses the exact \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) followed by one conditional Gram solve. Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026) supply the categorical inverse-feature product-bridge precursor, but not observed-data canonicality or the non-oracle projected-score remainder. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009), Hu and Schennach (2008), and Deaner (2023) inform latent-factor identification; their level-identification results do not furnish the measurable uniformly bounded DQM right inverse proved here. Tsiatis and Ma (2004) inform nuisance-score projection, Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016) inform coherent repeated-measurement estimation, and Tsybakov (2009) informs the smooth sieve benchmark. The implementation result does not assume access to a true measurement support or a true Gram rank; design-known supports are an optional specialization.
